projectSummary: Pectoralis major EMG characteristics change with humeral elevation angle. This is Q1c evidence in the frequency domain rather than the amplitude domain, so it demonstrates position dependence without quantifying a change in contribution to torque.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Mean frequency is a spectral property influenced by fibre conduction velocity, fatigue and electrode geometry; it is not a measure of force contribution.
Whole-muscle pectoralis sampling at a single electrode site, so no portion resolution.

study.intervention: standardised arm elevation at 90, 135 and 180 degrees
study.population: Surface EMG was recorded from the anterior, middle and posterior deltoid, infraspinatus, latissimus dorsi, serratus anterior, pectoralis major and the external obliques during a standardised arm-elevation strength test at 90, 135 and 180 degrees. Pectoralis major electrodes were placed in the neutral arm position 3.5 cm medial to the anterior axillary line. Twenty-four participants were tested in three groups of eight to distribute testing load.

title: Shoulder angle effects on neuromuscular activation and rapid force production: sEMG time-frequency and force-time analyses.
